leads.name: The Ginkgo of Paseo de Carmelitas

location.address: Paseo de Carmelitas at Calle Wences Moreno, Salamanca

leads.reason: Only about 45 years old (planted 1981-82 by MOPU during landscaping, 'landed by mistake' mixed in with cypresses), so it fails the age bar and has no notable girth. Nice footnote (first ginkgo planted in the city, nearly removed in a later renovation, saved by municipal gardeners, visited by Pharmacy/Biology students) but too young and too ordinary in stature to be worth the walk on its own. Keep as a lead in case a reader or a future pass finds it has grown into something more, or as filler if the city page needs an eighth tree later.

leads.name: The Calocedrus of Campo de San Francisco

location.address: Campo de San Francisco park, Salamanca, near the fountain and the historic library

leads.reason: Still only one source after a second pass (Salamancahoy, 2026-04-07): tallest tree in the park, a long clean trunk into a discreet crown, estimated 100-150 years old, said to have been walked past by Miguel de Unamuno without documented proof he ever noticed it. Checked and found nothing: es.wikipedia's Campo de San Francisco (Salamanca) article (no individual trees named, only a general note on 600+ poplars planted early), a 2015 local-history blog on the park's own tree losses (poplars, funerary cypresses, no calocedrus), and an iNaturalist search for Calocedrus decurrens near this coordinate (nearest observation is 3km away in Cabrerizos, a different tree). Not part of the Castilla y Leon regional register (that register's only Salamanca-city entry is the Escuelas Mayores sequoia, slm_001; see note below). No girth or exact in-park coordinate found. Needs either a second written source or a girth/coordinate a future pass can obtain in person or from a park map.

leads.name: The four laurels ('árbol del triunfo') of Campo de San Francisco

location.address: Campo de San Francisco park, Salamanca, forming a square among other trees

leads.reason: Salamanca's municipal government is preparing a NEW local catalogue of singular/heritage trees (33 elements total, announced 2026-07-10, distinct from the Castilla y Leon regional register), which is expected to include four notable laurel specimens forming a square in Campo de San Francisco, plus a laurel survivor of the old orchard at Huerto de Calixto y Melibea and others at Parque de los Jesuitas, Parque de Wurzburg and elsewhere. Not yet designated (catalogue still in preparation as of the source date), no individual ages, heights or girths published, and an ensemble of four ordinary-height (5-10m) laurels forming a square is a weak collectible point on its own. Worth re-checking once the municipal catalogue is actually adopted, since it may name/measure individual specimens then.

notes:
Verification pass 2026-09-11 (continuation). RESOLVED: the '16-tree catalog' question from the earlier pass. A 2013 blog post (arbolessingularescyl.blogspot.com/2010/07/provincia-de-salamanca.html) lists all 16 names in the Castilla y Leon regional 'Catalogo de especimenes vegetales de singular relevancia' (ORDEN MAM/1156/2006) tagged to Salamanca PROVINCE, and they match one-to-one against the 16 province=Salamanca entries already in data/registers/castilla-leon-arboles-notables.json (AS-SA-02,03,05,07,08,09,10,11,12,13,16,17,18,19,21,22). This is a PROVINCIAL catalogue, not a city one: only AS-SA-10 (Sequoia de la Universidad, already slm_001) sits in Salamanca city; the other 15 (Cedro de la Florida and Cipres de la Catedral in Ciudad Rodrigo, Cedro de la Francesa and a giant sequoia in Bejar's El Bosque estate, several oaks/pines/a beech/a yew/a lime scattered across La Alberca, Penacaballera, Herguijuela de la Sierra, Escurial de la Sierra, Fuentes de Onoro, Monforte, Tejeda y Segoyuela and Espeja) sit 70-90km from Salamanca city, well outside the ~30 minute day-trip boundary. Nothing further to chase here; do not re-run this hunt. Ecologistas en Accion's own list page (ecologistasenaccion.org/4098) still 403s to curl even with a browser user agent and has no Wayback snapshot (archive.org availability API returned an empty snapshot list on 2026-09-11), but it is now redundant since the blog post above already supplied the full 16-name list and it was cross-checked against the register.

Added this pass: slm_004, The Yew of Plaza de la Libertad (Taxus baccata), promoted out of this leads file after a second source (La Gaceta de Salamanca, 2026-09-10) confirmed it independently of the original 2019 SalamancaRTV mention and resolved that it is a DIFFERENT tree from the 4 yews around the Columbus statue in Parque de Colon (which are only ~30 years old per the same 2026-09-10 article).
